# Feasibility Report: Automated Lemmatization & Morphology of Swete’s Septuagint (LXX)

*Generated by an Antigravity 2.0 AI Agent on September 19, 2026*

**Date**: September 2026  
**Target Corpus**: Henry Barclay Swete, *The Old Testament in Greek according to the Septuagint* (1887–1912, reprint 1930)  
**Corpus Scale**: ~600,000 tokens | ~45,000 unique surface types | ~31,100 verses  
**Objective**: Produce a fully unencumbered, public-domain (US & Global) morphologically tagged Greek Old Testament corpus reaching **~98% accuracy**.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Generating a high-accuracy, FOSS morphological database for the Swete Septuagint is **highly feasible** with today’s hybrid NLP and AI toolchains. 

Because the Septuagint is almost identical in token count to the Flavius Josephus corpus (~500k vs. ~600k words), the architectural lessons from the **Josephus Reader** pipeline (`~/dev/2-tmp/josephus-reader/pipeline/`) directly apply. Furthermore, the LXX's simpler Hellenistic syntax and existing biblical treebanks (like PROIEL) make automated parsing even more dependable than Josephus's periodic literary Greek.

## 2. Core Strategy & Enhancements

### A. The Proper Name Heuristic (Capitalization & Gazetteer)
Your proposed heuristic significantly reduces pipeline complexity:
* **The Rule**: Any capitalized token that is **not sentence-initial** and lacks an unambiguous common Greek root is automatically routed to the **Proper Name Handler**.
* **Handling Declensions**:
  1. *Indeclinable Semitic Names* (e.g., Ἀβραάμ, Δαυίδ, Ἰακώβ, Ἰσραήλ): Automatically tagged as `ProperNoun | Indeclinable` with the lemma identical to the surface form.
  2. *Declinable Names* (e.g., Μωυσῆς / Μωυσέως, Ἱεροσόλυμα / Ἱerosολύμων): Grouped by common prefixes and human-audited using a compact gazetteer (~1,500 distinct biblical names).
* **Impact**: Eliminates false-positive verb/adjective root searches for ~40,000 name tokens (~6.5% of the total corpus).

### B. The 4-Tier Hybrid Pipeline Architecture

```
[Raw Swete Tokens (600k)]
         │
         ▼
[Tier 1: High-Precision Whitelist & Gazetteer]
  • Particles, prepositions, and indeclinable proper names
  • Resolves ~25% of tokens with 100% precision
         │
         ▼
[Tier 2: Dual-Engine Disambiguation]
  • Engine A: Morpheus C-cruncher (defines all valid grammatical forms)
  • Engine B: Stanza `grc_proiel` (neural model predicting context POS & features)
  • Agreement Intersection: Resolves ~68% of remaining tokens
  • Cumulative Accuracy: ~92–93%
         │
         ▼
[Tier 3: AI-Assisted Batch Triage (The Human Replacement)]
  • Targets the ~5–7% of tokens where Morpheus and Stanza conflict
  • De-duplicated into ~4,000 unique (context_sentence, token) pairs
  • Batched to LLM (Gemini 1.5 Flash / Claude Haiku) for zero-shot adjudication
  • Cumulative Accuracy: ~97.5%
         │
         ▼
[Tier 4: Offline CATSS Benchmark Oracle & Human Curation]
  • Automated script compares Swete output against CATSS Rahlfs alignment
  • Flags remaining discrepancies for targeted human review (~2,000–3,000 edge cases)
  • Cumulative Accuracy: ~98.5%+
```

## 3. Resource & Time Estimates to Reach ~98% Accuracy

### A. Computational Time & Infrastructure

| Pipeline Phase | Tool / Engine | Compute Resources | Estimated Run Time |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tokenization & Normalization** | Python (Regex + NFC) | Modern 8-core CPU | **< 30 seconds** |
| **Morpheus Candidate Generation** | `cruncher` (C/Flex) | Single thread | **~ 20 seconds** (on 45k unique types) |
| **Neural Context Tagging** | Stanza (`grc_proiel`) | Apple Silicon (MPS) or GPU<br>*(CPU fallback)* | **~ 8–12 minutes**<br>*(~ 45–60 minutes on CPU)* |
| **Constraint Solver / Intersect** | Python | Single thread | **< 1 minute** |
| **AI Batch Triage (~4,000 pairs)** | Async API (Gemini Flash) | Cloud API (100 parallel workers) | **~ 3–5 minutes** (Cost: < $1.50) |
| **CATSS Benchmark Comparison** | Python Diff Script | Single thread | **~ 30 seconds** |
| **Total Computational Time** | | | **~ 15–20 minutes** (GPU) / **~ 1 hour** (CPU) |

### B. Human Effort Estimates

Reaching standard automated quality (~92%) requires zero human intervention. Moving from **92% to ~98%** requires targeted human-in-the-loop validation:

| Task | Scope | Human Time Estimate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Proper Name Gazetteer Curation** | Reviewing and approving the list of ~1,500 unique biblical names and their declension patterns | **2 – 3 hours** |
| **2. Common Overrides & Normalization Table** | Reviewing top 200 frequent ambiguous words (e.g., εἰς vs. εἷς, ὅτι, ὥστε) | **1 – 2 hours** |
| **3. Reviewing AI Triage Disagreements** | Spot-checking low-confidence LLM decisions and difficult hapax legomena | **3 – 4 hours** |
| **4. CATSS Diff Cluster Analysis** | Inspecting systematic divergences between Swete and CATSS (identifying textual variants vs. parsing errors) | **2 – 3 hours** |
| **Total Human Effort** | | **8 – 12 hours total** |

## 4. Risks & Mitigations

1. **Textual Divergences (Swete vs. Rahlfs/CATSS)**:
   * *Risk*: When benchmarking against CATSS, differences in underlying manuscripts (Vaticanus B in Swete vs. eclectic text in Rahlfs) will show up as "errors."
   * *Mitigation*: The benchmark script must first align verses and ignore word-mismatches, comparing only where surface forms are identical or cognate.
2. **Homographs (Accents & Breathing)**:
   * *Risk*: Ancient Greek has words differing only by accentuation (e.g., τίς interrogative vs. τις indefinite).
   * *Mitigation*: Swete’s text is fully accented, allowing accent-sensitive disambiguation rules to eliminate over 50% of nominal/pronominal ambiguities before neural tagging.
